business_summary: Varun Beverages operates in the beverages sector. The evidence supplied covers financial metrics only, with no description of products, geographies or customers, so this summary stays at sector level. FY25 net profit was 3036.49 Rs cr and trailing four-quarter net profit was 3386.14 Rs cr, with no loss-making quarters in the last four.
why_own: The case rests on sustained growth (revenue 18.08% 3y CAGR, net profit 26.57% 3y CAGR) delivered with a 23.38% operating margin, 19.04% ROCE and low leverage (0.13x debt/equity). Evidence is financial only, with no results or call documents, so the drivers are metric-based and the qualitative side of the thesis is untested.

drivers.statement: Revenue keeps compounding at a double-digit rate: 3y revenue CAGR is 18.08%, below the 5y CAGR of 27.44%.
Operating margin holds at a high level: 23.38% in FY25, up 1.65 pp over three years.
Returns on capital stay healthy: ROCE is 19.04% and ROE is 16.78%.
The balance sheet stays conservative: debt/equity is 0.13x and interest cover is 21.46x. (warn line tightened by code from 0.5 to 0.17.)

kill_criteria.description: Operating margin falls below 18%, well under the current 23.38%.
Leverage rises above 1.0x debt/equity from the current 0.13x.
3y revenue CAGR falls below 8%, against 18.08% now.

risks.statement: Valuation stays demanding: trailing P/E is 39.96x and price/book is 6.91x. P/E is 30.39% below its own 5y median of 57.4x, but a high multiple leaves little room if growth slows.
Growth is slower than earlier: 3y revenue CAGR of 18.08% compares with 27.44% over 5 years. The reason is untested here, and further slowing would weaken the growth case.

Margin and return levels (operating margin 23.38%, ROCE 19.04%) are already high, so any reversal would hit earnings growth. Net profit 3y CAGR is 26.57%, and profit compounding relies on these levels holding.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis is wrong if growth keeps slowing and margins slip while the market still pays about 40x earnings. Revenue 3y CAGR is already 18.08% against 27.44% over 5 years, and the reason is untested. The thresholds are lenient: growth must halve to 8-10% and margin fall about 5 pp to 18% before anything trips. Net profit compounds at 26.57%, faster than revenue, but operating margin gained only 1.65 pp, so the extra profit growth is not explained by the evidence. P/E at 39.96x and P/B at 6.91x sit against ROE of 16.78%. The 'discount' is to a 57.4x median that was itself rich. No documents back the qualitative case. What would change this view: Evidence that the 3y-versus-5y slowdown is a base effect or a one-off, together with documents showing what drives the margin and the faster profit growth, would remove most of the objection.
